title: Greek Moussaka
subtitle: Layered lamb, aubergine, and béchamel bake
excerpt: The great Greek baked dish: layers of fried aubergine, spiced minced lamb, and a thick, eggy béchamel sauce baked until golden and set. Unlike the simpler Balkan versions, the Greek moussaka has that thick custard topping that makes it something between a bake and a terrine.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moussaka is eaten across the Eastern Mediterranean and Middle East in various forms; the Greek version with its thick béchamel topping was largely codified in the early twentieth century by Nikolaos Tselementes, a Greek chef trained in France who adapted the Ottoman dish with the French sauce to create the layered, baked version now known internationally as Greek moussaka. The dish requires several stages of preparation: the aubergines are sliced and fried or roasted to remove moisture and bitterness; the lamb sauce is cooked with tomato, cinnamon, and allspice (the characteristic sweet-spiced note of Greek meat dishes); and the béchamel is enriched with eggs and set very thick. The assembled dish is baked and rested before cutting; a freshly-assembled moussaka collapses when cut.

content.text: Salting the aubergine slices and leaving them for 30 minutes draws out moisture and reduces oil absorption during frying. The béchamel must be very thick: it should hold its shape when spread. Make the dish a day ahead: it slices much more cleanly after an overnight rest in the refrigerator, and the flavours deepen considerably.

items.preparation: sliced 1 cm thick; salted for 30 minutes; rinsed and dried

content.text: Fry the aubergine slices in batches in olive oil until deep golden on both sides. Drain on kitchen paper. For the meat sauce, cook the onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon of oil until soft. Add the lamb and brown. Add the wine, tomatoes, tomato puree, cinnamon, and allspice. Simmer for 30 minutes until thick.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Stir over medium heat until very thick. Remove from the heat, cool slightly, then stir in the beaten eggs. Season.

Heat the oven to 180°C / fan 160°C / gas 4. Layer the aubergines in a large baking dish. Pour the lamb sauce over. Spread the béchamel over the top in a thick even layer. Scatter over the parmesan. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 20 minutes before cutting.
